terms.gloss: the young of an animal: a kitten
evidence: M-O s.v. cub, puppy, kitten, young (of most mammals)
terms.comment: The word for the young of any animal, a whelp or cub, used of a cat’s young by Phaedrus (Lewis & Short); without a context it means a puppy (see “puppy”), so say catulus fēlis where it matters. Of a cat having kittens, parere.

phrases.latin: Fēlēs nostra catulōs peperit: quīnque sunt!
phrases.english: Our cat has had kittens: there are five!

phrases.latin: Catulum lēniter tenē; adhūc parvulus est.
phrases.english: Hold the kitten gently; he’s still very little.

phrases.latin: aquila in sublīmī quercū nīdum fēcerat; fēlēs cavernam nancta in mediā pepererat
phrases.english: an eagle had built her nest at the top of an oak; a cat had found a hollow halfway up and had her kittens there

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. cub, puppy, kitten, young (of most mammals).
